practice_span: I have worked with my father since I was eleven. It has now been forty-five years.
craft_description: I say they are toys carved in light wood and painted. To children I say, these are toys with life.
craft_distinct: The wood is very light and the kitta coating makes the surface smooth. One person can carry even a large figure.
motif_meaning: The parrot. It means good luck and speech. Green and red feel the truest colours.
motif_story: I made a pair of parrots for a wedding. The bride's grandmother said, I had the same at my wedding.
colour_change: Earlier stone and plant colours. Now acrylic. The way we paint eyes is the same.
specialisation: Painting a toy's eyes. I made a new small bird set.
known_for: I am called to paint the eyes of the goddess figure for the village fair.
craft_keep_change: I would keep hand carving. I would change waiting for money after fairs.
local_belonging_phrase: “The name of Kinnala is itself the mark of a Kinnala toy. They say our elders did this same work from the time of Hampi.”
place_belonging_feeling: The name of our village, Kinnala, is the mark of our toys. That is the pride.
ecological_input: Light soft wood used to come from the surrounding hills. Tamarind seed paste and the dry sun help the toys dry.
place_use_moment: I dried tamarind seeds in the sun, pounded them into paste and applied it to a toy.
place_missing: Without the light wood the toy becomes heavy, and carving is harder.
place_change: Cutting trees now needs permission, and there are fewer trees in the hills. Mining has raised the dust, and the boys go to Bengaluru.
place_before_after: Earlier wood came from the hills; now it needs permission, and there are fewer trees.
emotion_about_place_change: “Without trees, where will toys come from? It feels like we must go and plant trees ourselves.”
teacher_name_relation: My father, Hanumappa Chitragar. My aunt taught me the painting.
teaching_memory: My father took a horse I had carved, closed his eyes and felt it. He said, “The horse isn't running.” After I bent the neck a little, he smiled.
remembered_phrase_gesture: “A toy's life is in its eyes.” As he said it, he held up a small brush between two fingers.
family_generations: My grandfather, my father, me. My son Manjunath carves, and my daughter-in-law Lakshmi paints. My grandson goes to school.
family_line: Grandfather → father Hanumappa → me → son Manjunath and daughter-in-law Lakshmi.
transmission_strength:
The children of the house quickly learn small toys, birds and fruit.

The large festival deity figures and the old way of applying kitta. There isn't much demand for it now.
teaching_practice: First I have them carve a small fruit, then a bird, and last a horse.
teaching_scene: We sat in the courtyard. I put the chisel in Lakshmi's hand and showed her the grain of the wood.
teaching_difficulty: Plastic toys are cheap. Learning takes years and pay isn't certain, so boys don't come.
primary_material:
Light soft wood, tamarind seed paste, kitta (a mix of sawdust and paste), paints.

Wood from Koppal and nearby hills. Tamarind seed from the village. Paints from the Hosapete market.
first_contact: I sat beside my father pounding tamarind seed. I still remember the sour smell of that paste.
material_special: This wood is light and soft to carve. So even a large figure can be carried by one person. Kitta makes the surface smooth.
material_in_hands: Good wood gives small shavings under the chisel and doesn't split. Kitta sticks to the finger but comes off easily.
material_spoke: Green wood sticks to the chisel and cracks after drying. If kitta dries to powder, it doesn't hold.
correction_action: I dry green wood in the shade for months. If a crack comes, I fill it with kitta and give a coat of lime.
piece_time: Two days for a bird, a month for a large figure. Never rush drying the wood.
material_change: Acrylic paint has replaced colours from stone and plants.
material_change_reason: The old colours take time to make, and few people know how.
material_change_gain:
Acrylic paint is bright, dries fast and lasts. Outside customers like it.

The soft glow of the old paints made from stone and plants is gone. Few people know how to make them.
occasion_of_use:
Figures for village fairs and deity festivals. Also toys for the Navaratri doll display.

On the fair's night, the sound of drums, the smell of camphor, and a toy's eye glinting in the lamplight.
use_importance: “When a Kinnala toy comes home, the child doesn't cry.” My grandmother used to say this.
use_feelings: Making the fair's figure, there is devotion and pride.
special_vs_everyday: Everyday toys and fruit can be sold to anyone. A fair's deity figure is made only at the village's request.
special_object_rule: While making a deity figure we fast, and the eyes are painted on the last day. After that, the figure isn't kept at home.
special_missing: Without the goddess figure there is no festival for the village.
not_for_sale_example: The goddess figure made for the village fair, and the old colour recipe from my grandfather's time.
why_protected: The figure belongs to the village, not to me. The recipe is the mark of our house. If it goes out, our work loses its value.
safer_alternative: Birds, horses and Dashavatara toys. Photos of them and video of the carving can be shown.
pride_source: Children not wanting to let go of my toys is my pride.
pride_moment: At Hampi Utsav a child would not let go of my toy and threw a tantrum. There were plastic toys right beside it.
recognition_by_others: The village elders called me to paint the eyes of the fair's figure. There is no greater honour.
loss_if_stopped: Light wood carving and the kitta method would go. It would be like the village losing its own name.
loss_picture: Plastic toys in every house, and no sound of chisels in the village.
key_stakeholder_of_loss: The Chitragar families of Kinnala, and the surrounding villages that need figures for their fairs.
craft_hours: Seven hours a day, including making the paste. Before Navaratri we work at night too.
change_in_lifetime: Before, fair work was the most. Now it is small gift toys, and sales through government fairs.
artisan_initiated_change: I taught carving to my daughter-in-law and made a new small bird set. I am also inviting school children to workshops.
desired_keep:
Hand carving, the kitta method, and the rules of the fair's figure.

Waiting months for money after a fair, and the idea that women should only paint.
strength_anchor: My hand is steady at painting a toy's eyes. When I touch wood, I know whether it is right.
concern_anchor: Good wood is getting hard to find, and new boys are not coming to learn the work.
shareable_content:
The carving method, the bird set, my name, the children's workshop.

The old colour recipe, the rites of the fair's figure, and the village's internal matters.
desired_change:
Easier permission for wood, and schools asking for wooden toys instead of plastic.

The fair's figure will be made in the village, by hand, by the old rules.
learning_story: Once in a hurry I made fifty toys from green wood. In the Delhi cold they all cracked. I gave the money back. Now I don't lift a chisel until the wood is dry.
emotional_story: In my father's last year his hand shook. He gave me the brush for the fair's figure. When I painted the eyes, he stood up and bowed.
clarification_story:
Someone asked, this price for one bird? I gave it to them to lift. “So light?” they said. I told them that lightness takes six months of drying the wood.

People believe this is only children's toys. These same hands make the goddess figure for the fair.
